title: The recovery table count of the source and the table count of the Ownership Map do not agree
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3.docx
section: 2. What the sandbox seeds; 6. Counts the build checks
description: Version 3 counts 92 recovery tables and 4 extension tables in one recovery schema. The Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables holds 93 rows, of which 4 are the extension tables and 6 are the platform library tables. 92 plus 4 is 96, so the two counts differ by three tables and no source document reconciles them. The version 4 text keeps both counts as printed and does not state a total.
evidence: Version 3 section 6: Recovery tables 92; Extension tables 4. Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: 93 data rows; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json tables: 93 entries (4 extension tables, 6 platform library tables).
proposed: Let the Ownership Map sheet Tables govern ownership for all 93 tables and keep the 92 and 4 of version 3 as printed; the per-service DB stories of RWB-PLT-NF06 and the 19 service DB stories reconcile the counts when the schemas are built.

title: rwb-valuation owns no table, so the plan does not say where a route decision is kept
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
description: Sheet Tables assigns no table to S1 rwb-valuation: valuation_ext belongs to P1 and the version 3 recovery table valuation is one of the 20 removed tables. The test data plan therefore cannot seed a valuation schema. The inputs are in rwb_source_data and the outcome has no stated home.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: no row with owner S1; sheet Services: S1 rwb-valuation, wave 3, schema rwb_valuation. Version 3 section 2: valuation among the 20 tables that do not exist.
proposed: Seed the valuation inputs in rwb_source_data (valuation_ext) and the RouteDecided outcome as a decision record in rwb_decision; the valuation schema holds only the platform library objects until a technical specification adds a table.

title: No source states which product hosts the contract fakes
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: Architecture v5 slide 11 and slide 20 make every service publish its OpenAPI 3.1, AsyncAPI 3.0 and activity contract jar before its code, and Template and Rules R5.4 has the consumer build against the published contract and its fake. No source names the product, service or environment that hosts the fakes for this programme.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11: every service publishes its contracts (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, activity jar) before code; contract tests run in every build. Template and Rules v1 R5.4: class C, build against the published contract and its fake. No source names a mock product.
proposed: Use any stub server that is generated from the published artefact and runs in the pipeline; the choice belongs to the CON story of each provider and is not made in this document.

title: The source does not say how the data in a fake relates to the sandbox seed
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3.docx
description: Version 3 seeds one data set and reads source data through views. With 19 services, a consumer test uses a fake instead of the provider, so the two sides must agree on the business keys. No source states whether a fake carries its own data, a copy of the seed or the same key set.
evidence: Version 3 section 2: the sandbox is the only test data set below SIT. Template and Rules v1 R5.4: class C, build against the published contract and its fake. Architecture v5 slide 11: contract tests run in every build.
proposed: One key set (caseId, accountId, partyKey) is shared by the seed and every fake; each fake is loaded from the seed file of its provider and reloaded when the seed changes, so no second data set exists.

title: The plan does not say which service applies the mask once the masking rules are rwb-access data
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3.docx
description: Version 3 says masking follows RWB-E1-037 and that Compliance sets the rules, the version and the position as data. The Ownership Map puts masking_rule in rwb-access (P4) and every personal field is now read through rwb-source-data (P1) and displayed by the owning service. Which service applies which mask is not stated.
evidence: Version 3 section 4: the rules, the masking version and the masking position are data. Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: masking_rule owned by P4. Architecture v5 slide 46: masking is applied by rwb-source-data.
proposed: rwb-access holds the approved masking version; rwb-source-data applies the mask at the 30 views; display masking at the API is applied by the service that owns the field, under the same version.

title: Which service seeds which rows of the shared case set is not specified
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3.docx
description: Version 3 seeds one schema from one generator. After the split, the 2,812 cases and their linked rows belong to several schemas. No source states the order, the owner or the interface by which one service's seed refers to another service's row.
evidence: Version 3 section 2: it seeds rows by reading sys_objects, sys_fields and lov_value. Architecture v5 slide 29: each service owns its schema and no cross-schema key. Template and Rules v1 R5.4 DP-01.
proposed: Each service seeds its own schema from its own baseline with seed 20261128 and no service seeds another's schema; the case rows are seeded once, in rwb_case, and the other schemas reference them by plain key.

title: Events that the event catalogue does not number cannot be named by an EV ID in a fake
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md
description: The Ownership Map holds 30 numbered events (EV-01 to EV-30). Architecture v5 slide 43 adds further events without a number: RouteDecided, AssetSold, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult, TreatmentClosed, GuaranteeClaimFiled, GuaranteeClaimSettled, AccountsTransferred, AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged, FileDelivered and FileFailed. A Kafka fake of those providers has an event name and a topic but no EV ID to cite.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Events: 30 rows, EV-01 to EV-30. Architecture v5 slide 43: the rows marked + carry no number.
proposed: Name each of those fakes by event name and topic in this plan; the number is added by the owner of the event catalogue and propagated to the fake when it exists.

title: The daily journey smoke workflow has no data set in the plan
source: 09 Testing and quality/Recovery Workbench Test Data Plan v3.docx
description: Architecture v5 slide 46 and slide 44 put a daily journey smoke workflow (JOB-22, PlatformSmokeWorkflow) in the platform, and it crosses the services in one journey. Version 3 lists the data for eleven tests but not for the smoke run.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 46: a daily journey smoke workflow (JOB-22). Ownership Map v1 sheet Jobs: JOB-22 Smoke workflow, owner PLT, 06:00. Version 3 section 3: eleven tests, none of them the smoke run.
proposed: The smoke run uses the DEV seed of all 19 schemas and the fakes; it creates its own case per journey step and leaves the seed of the other tests untouched.

title: The map gives six tables to the platform library but does not say which schema holds them
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx
section: 2. What the sandbox seeds; 2.1 Rows per schema (row PLT)
description: Sheet Tables assigns six tables to PLT: outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event, idempotency_key, feature_flag and feature_flag_change. PLT is not one of the 19 services and owns no schema, so the test data plan cannot seed them from a service row. Architecture v5 slide 20 puts the outbox and inbox in every service schema and says nothing about the two feature-flag tables.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: six rows with owner PLT. Sheet Services: 19 services, none of them PLT. Architecture v5 slide 20: DB own schema: business tables + outbox + inbox + decision_record.
proposed: Create the four outbox, inbox and idempotency objects in all 19 schemas, as DP-09 requires, and keep feature_flag and feature_flag_change once, in rwb_integration, which serves the feature-flag admin API; the seed treats the four as per-schema tables.
